title: The Three Tradesmen
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: The citizens of a certain city were debating about the best material to use in the fortifications which were about to be erected for the greater security of the town. A Carpenter got up and advised the use of wood, which he said was readily procurable and easily worked. A Stone-mason objected to wood on the ground that it was so inflammable, and recommended stones instead. Then a Tanner got on his legs and said, "In my opinion there's nothing like leather." Every man for himself.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what were the citizens debating about?
options: The best material to use in the fortifications
Which tradesman should lead the city
How to fund a new marketplace
Whether to go to war with a neighboring city

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why were the fortifications being erected?
options: For the greater security of the town
To celebrate a recent victory
To impress a visiting ruler
To replace an older, ruined wall

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what material did the Carpenter advise using?
options: Stone
Leather
Wood
Brick

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did the Carpenter favor wood?
options: It was readily procurable and easily worked
It was the cheapest material available
It had been used in the old fortifications
It was the strongest material he knew of

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did the Stone-mason object to using wood?
options: It was too expensive to buy in quantity
It was too heavy to transport
It was so inflammable
It attracted insects

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what exact words does the Tanner say?
options: "Stone is the only sensible choice"
"In my opinion there's nothing like leather"
"Wood will serve us well enough"
"We should use all three materials together"

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "inflammable" mean in "it was so inflammable"?
options: Easily set on fire
Difficult to shape
Prone to rotting quickly
Too expensive to obtain

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the closing line, "Every man for himself"?
options: Each tradesman recommended the material tied to his own trade rather than the town's true needs
The citizens ultimately agreed on a single best material
Only the Tanner's advice was taken seriously
The fortifications were never built because of the disagreement

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who spoke first in the debate?
options: The Tanner
The Carpenter
The Stone-mason
A citizen without a trade

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what material did the Stone-mason recommend instead of wood?
options: Stones
Leather
Iron
Clay

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the Tanner's opinion about the best material?
options: That there's nothing like leather
That leather should only be used for minor repairs
That the Carpenter was right about wood
That the debate should be settled by a vote

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "procurable" mean in "readily procurable and easily worked"?
options: Able to be obtained
Able to withstand fire
Pleasant to look at
Difficult to transport

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what pattern connects each tradesman's recommendation?
options: Each man recommended the material connected to his own trade
Each man recommended a material he personally disliked
Each man agreed with the tradesman who spoke before him
Each man recommended the cheapest available option

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Carpenter, a Stone-mason, and a Tanner each urge the city to build its fortifications from the material their own trade supplies
A city council votes unanimously to build its fortifications from stone
A Carpenter and a Stone-mason come to blows over which material to use
The city abandons its fortification plans after hearing the debate
